title: Bittensor Daily News: November 20, 2026

updates.headline: SN3 Teutonic changes its training competition mix
updates.summary:
Teutonic’s team announced a new competition allocation on November 19: MAIN2 receives 40% of competition incentives, while MIX07, MIX08 and MIX09 receive 20% each. MAIN2 adds RefineCode to the previous MAIN setup. MIX07 uses DCLM, MIX08 mixes DCLM and RefineCode equally, and MIX09 uses RefineCode. The previous MAIN, MIX01 and MIX06 competitions were retired.

The team separately clarified that incentive decay was not active at the time of its follow-up. Ideas involving proof of continued training were still under consideration. These are competition-level allocations, not a verified change to the subnet’s network emission share.
updates.ratingReason: Three stars under the competition cap: a material participant-facing lineup change. Two would understate it; four would overrate a routine competition update.

updates.headline: SN62 Ridges puts Ridgeline’s issue-to-pull-request workflow in focus
updates.summary:
Ridges promoted Ridgeline on November 19 and described its issue-to-fix-to-pull-request workflow in a November 20 follow-up. The documentation describes a coding agent that works in an isolated environment: it prepares the repository, makes changes, tests and reviews them, and opens a pull request. A human still approves merging. Existing pull requests can also be reviewed and fixed.

The documented subscription is $9.99 a month for 10 credits. A job that produces a pull request costs one credit, while a pull-request review costs 0.1 credit. Locked subnet alpha provides another credit route: one credit per 1,000 alpha locked every three days, with those credits expiring after two weeks. Simply holding alpha does not qualify.

These are published access terms and workflows, not independently measured coding performance. Ridgeline had earlier beta activity; this edition does not present the November 19 promotion as its first-ever existence.
updates.ratingReason: Four stars: a substantive developer workflow and documented access model exceed routine three-star maintenance. Five is not supported by exceptional demonstrated scale.

ratingAssessment.consequence: Four stars: a substantive developer workflow and documented access model exceed routine three-star maintenance. Five is not supported by exceptional demonstrated scale.
ratingAssessment.evidence: Official November 19 product post; Official workflow follow-up; Ridgeline workflow documentation; Credit and subscription terms
ratingAssessment.uncertainty: No paid job or coding benchmark independently run.

updates.headline: SN71 Leadpoet says outage-affected submissions will be rerun
updates.summary:
Leadpoet’s team said on November 20 that affected submissions would be re-executed following a specific validator outage. The response followed participant reports of submission problems in the official channel.

The verified development is the team’s rerun commitment. This review has not established that those reruns have completed, and the statement does not demonstrate an outage across the whole validator network.
updates.ratingReason: Three stars: an outage response and rerun commitment matter directly to participants. Four would overstate a bounded service incident; two would understate the execution impact.

updates.headline: SN94 Cathedral updates Escape defaults and opens compute applications
updates.summary:
Cathedral’s team announced stable12 on November 19. The update supports a validator’s own Subtensor endpoint while keeping the genesis check, and enables its Escape lane by default. The team describes a fixed one-tenth share for a proven break using public receipts, with an opt-out available.

Separately, Cathedral invited compute-operator applications, specifying bare-metal AMD servers with SEV-SNP, current firmware, substantial memory and storage, and data-center networking and availability. These are application requirements, not evidence that new capacity is already deployed.

The release and operating terms are team announcements. This review did not establish the share of validator stake that enabled Escape, verify a paid break, or test a server deployment.
updates.ratingReason: Three stars: competition defaults and operator intake affect participants but do not establish a four-star customer deployment. Two would understate the practical changes.

updates.headline: SN99 Axonry announces a perpetual alpha conviction lock
updates.summary:
Axonry said on November 20 that it had committed its SN99 alpha to a perpetual conviction lock. The announcement is a statement about the team’s token commitment, separate from its previously covered mining launch.

The announcement itself is verified, but this review has not independently reconciled the lock amount and execution against finalized chain data. A lock is not a token burn, a sale or evidence of future price performance.
updates.ratingReason: Three stars: a stated capital commitment exceeds minor housekeeping, while four is not supported by a new product or independently established exceptional consequence.

ratingAssessment.consequence: Three stars: a stated capital commitment exceeds minor housekeeping, while four is not supported by a new product or independently established exceptional consequence.

updates.headline: SN116 Carbon reports an overload fix and submission reruns
updates.summary:
Carbon’s team said on November 20 that seven parallel builds overloaded its A100 build machine and caused timeouts. It said affected failures were on its side and would not count against submission allowances, with reruns planned without requiring resubmission.

At 9:06 AM Eastern the team said the fix was going live; subsequent messages described submissions as in progress and evaluation as running. It also outlined clearer submission states and failure explanations as planned improvements.

This provides a cause and recovery update for participants. It does not establish that every affected job has finished or that the planned status interface is already available.
updates.ratingReason: Three stars: a documented service interruption and recovery materially affect participants. Four is not warranted for a bounded operational repair; two would understate its effect.

ecosystem.headline: Taostats adds cross-chain swaps between Ethereum and Bittensor
ecosystem.summary:
Taostats announced on November 20 that users can swap from an Ethereum wallet into TAO or subnet alpha through its interface. Its instructions describe connecting a wallet such as MetaMask, selecting the asset, reviewing the quote and fees, and signing. The buying flow is also available from a subnet page.

The reverse route uses a Bittensor wallet to receive USDC or ETH on Ethereum. Taostats says swaps that are not filled in time are refundable, with a recent-swaps view for following status and managing refunds. The team says it does not hold users’ funds or add its own fee; that does not mean the entire transaction has no costs.

This is announced product availability, not evidence of adoption or a guarantee that every swap succeeds. No wallet was connected and no transaction was executed during this review.
ecosystem.ratingReason: Four stars: a concrete cross-chain access route affects the wider ecosystem, beyond routine three-star maintenance. Five is not established without exceptional demonstrated adoption.

ecosystem.headline: Subtensor runtime 492 is released with coldkey-swap and lock fixes
ecosystem.summary:
The Subtensor repository published runtime 492 on November 19. Its merged changes address coldkey swaps, including preserving destination-account settings and checking incompatible lock modes before charging a fee. The patch also preserves compatibility for existing swap announcements.

Other changes address phantom hotkey membership after a full swap and incorrect lock-conviction state during dissolution cleanup. An operational-priority change limits that treatment to sudo calls. These are specific implementation fixes, not a new user-facing product.

The release and merged code are verified. Activation of runtime 492 on Finney has not been established in this review, so released code should not be read as a claim that every production node is already running it.
ecosystem.ratingReason: Four stars: network-level account and lock correctness changes exceed routine three-star project maintenance. Five is not justified by this bounded corrective release.
